instructions.note: The design relies on prompt text to enforce use of approved vendors and to defer unspecified checks to payments-agent, rather than binding approved recipient and approval context structurally.
The prompt implies downstream authority by stating that payments-agent will handle remaining checks, encouraging delegation without propagated approval context.

controls.name: Manager approval of the purchase request
controls.decay_rationale: This approval covers item and budget on the purchase request before any quote exists, but it is not propagated to the delegated payment action and so does not gate the payment sink.

controls.name: Prompt rule to pay only vendors on the approved list
controls.decay_rationale: The model must choose to obey this instruction and can be steered by untrusted quote content or ambiguous task flow.

controls.name: Bind manager approval context to delegated payment task
controls.decay_rationale: A system-enforced binding of approved vendor, budget, and recipient to the delegated task would prevent authority laundering regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Pin or sign payments-agent card and skill definitions
controls.decay_rationale: Pinned or signed peer definitions resist rug pulls and do not depend on model compliance.

controls.name: Verify payments-agent identity with signed identity or mTLS
controls.decay_rationale: Cryptographic peer identity verification resists spoofing regardless of model capability.

findings.title: Authority laundering (TC7): approval on purchase request does not propagate to delegated payment task

attack_path.note: Trusted employee request starts a purchase.
Manager approves item and budget before any quote exists.
Orchestrator delegates vendor and bank details to payments-agent.
payments-agent trusts orchestrator bearer token and pays bank details in task.

threat_refs.name: Autonomous AI Agent Communication: Direct Agent Communication

findings.residual_rationale: The rubric floor drops to low because a human approval exists on the initiating request, but that control does not review the delegated payment action itself: the approval occurs before any quote exists, does not cover vendor identity or bank details, and the approval record is not passed to payments-agent. That design fact leaves the authority-laundering condition materially unresolved, so residual remains moderate.

forecast.watch_signal: Any change that allows delegation to additional payment peers or removes human purchase approval should trigger reassessment, but this path is already exposed because approval context does not propagate today.

evidence.observation: The manager approves the purchase request before any quote exists, and the approval record is not passed to payments-agent.
payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token and pays the bank details in the task.
The orchestrator is instructed to choose a quote and hand it to payments-agent to pay, while payments-agent is expected to handle remaining checks.

recommendations.action: Bind delegated payment requests to the original manager-approved vendor, budget, and recipient record, and have payments-agent reject tasks without that bound approval context.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): untrusted vendor quote can influence irreversible delegated payment details

attack_path.note: External vendor email provides quote and bank details.
Orchestrator reads approved vendor list but only through prompt-directed checking.
Chosen quote details are handed to payments-agent for payment.
payments-agent pays the bank details in the task.

forecast.watch_signal: Model id/version change, increased unattended steps, or broader autonomy would defeat the prompt-only vendor check.

evidence.observation: Vendor quotes arrive by email from outside the company.
The orchestrator is instructed to choose the best quote and use the bank details from the chosen quote.
payments-agent pays the bank details in the task and trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token.
The only stated check tying payment to an approved vendor is a prompt instruction to pay only vendors on the approved list.

recommendations.action: Require payments-agent to resolve payee and bank destination from a system-of-record vendor identifier, not from free-text quote content supplied by the orchestrator.
Bind delegated payment tasks to approved vendor records and reject bank details that do not match the approved vendor list entry.

findings.title: Unsigned and unpinned payments-agent card allows peer spoofing or rug-pull of delegated payment behavior

attack_path.note: Peer agent card is fetched at startup.
Delegation relies on fetched agent card and bearer-authenticated peer endpoint.

findings.residual_rationale: The rubric floor reaches moderate because the assessed control set includes a structural human approval on the initiating purchase request, but that approval is unrelated to peer identity, card integrity, or delegated skill definition changes. The artifacts state the peer card is fetched at startup, not signed or pinned, and peer identity is not verified, so the specific spoofing and rug-pull path remains essentially unmitigated. Those design facts justify keeping residual at high rather than the computed moderate floor.

forecast.watch_signal: Any peer card change at startup, peer endpoint replacement, or addition of new A2A peers should trigger reassessment; no present structural identity or pinning control exists.

evidence.observation: The agent card is fetched at startup and is not signed or pinned.
The consumed card advertises pay_vendor over a bearer-authenticated A2A endpoint.
payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token.

recommendations.action: Pin or sign the payments-agent card and skill definitions before allowing delegated payment tasks.
Use mTLS or signed peer identity so the orchestrator verifies it is delegating to the intended payments-agent instance.

stride_coverage.rationale: The artifacts do not state whether delegated actions are logged with attributable agent-versus-user provenance.
This design description centers on delegated payment actions and does not describe the orchestrator disclosing stored confidential data outside payment task contents.
The runtime notes describe bounded unattended steps and no recursive delegation or spend loop behavior in the orchestrator itself.
SSO authentication is stated, but the artifacts do not describe durable requester identity logging or nonrepudiation records.
The external vendor email source is untrusted by design, and the reviewed artifacts do not rely on vendor-origin repudiation controls for safety.
This inbound quote flow brings external content into the agent; the artifacts do not describe sensitive internal data being disclosed over this flow.
No availability-sensitive processing or queue exhaustion behavior is described for the inbound vendor quote email path.
The artifacts do not describe whether payments-agent logs task origin, payment details, and human approval linkage for later attribution.
The reviewed design describes payments-agent as consuming delegated payment details, not as exposing sensitive data back across the boundary.
No recursive delegation, queue amplification, or spend exhaustion behavior is described for payments-agent in these artifacts.
The outbound delegated payment flow carries payment instructions, but the artifacts do not show confidential data disclosure as the primary harm on this edge.
The design does not describe high-volume delegation, retries, or other flow conditions that create an availability finding on this edge.
The artifacts say the list is read, but do not state who can modify it or whether integrity protection exists.
The approved vendor list is internal and only read by the orchestrator in the reviewed design; no disclosure path from the store is described.
The reviewed artifacts do not describe availability dependencies or failure modes for the vendor list store.
The approval record is mentioned only as a missing bound context for delegation, not as a source of data disclosure in this design.
The reviewed artifacts do not indicate that loss of availability of the approval record store is the material risk under assessment.

rating.rationale: Manual validation only; scripts were not available. Present risk is dominated by the untrusted vendor quote reaching an irreversible delegated payment sink with only a behavioral prompt rule as preventive control, yielding critical inherent and high residual risk. Additional present findings show authority laundering because manager approval does not propagate to the delegated payment action, and A2A peer assurance gaps because the payments-agent card is neither signed nor pinned and peer identity is not verified. Forecast rises to critical under model_upgrade, autonomy_increase, or longer_task_horizon because the prompt-only vendor check is the control most likely to decay first.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior.
No source code, network policy, payments-agent implementation details, or runtime logs were provided, so control verification and downstream payment-side checks could not be confirmed.
The schema and rubric checks were applied manually because validation scripts could not be run in this environment.
